scope: Proposition 7.2 of the manuscript “Weil classes and Hodge classes on abelian powers” (preprints/Weil-classes-and-Hodge-classes-on-abelian-powers-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 032 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c035db86eb706573), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 69. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are a class α ∈ H2(Y0, µr), a coherent α-twisted sheaf B of rank r with det B ≃ OY0 , and an invertible q∗α-twisted sheaf L on M, such that q∗ B ≃ E ⊗ L. (7.4) Let Y0 be the µr-gerbe of α. For every integer i, this isomorphism induces Exti Y0 (B, B) ≃ Exti M (E, E)Ḡ , Exti 0(B, B) ≃ Exti 0(E, E)Ḡ , (7.5) where the subscript 0 denotes the kernel of the perfect trace to Hi(O). Put λH = adet E r = tr(aE) r . Under the first isomorphism ϕ in degree two, the raw Hodge square Ext2 (B, B) ϕ − − → Ext2 (E, E)Ḡ  yσB  ye−λH σE H−2(Y0) q∗ − − → H−2(M) (7.6) commutes, both on full Ext and on its trace-free summand. In particular, full invariant injectivity for E makes B semiregular. By Lemma 7.1, full invariant injectivity for G is sufficient for this conclusion.
